description: Agent Reliability: submit a service’s degradation behavior record with the behavior it advertises for partial failure: the record with the service, each degraded mode it holds, the longest data is served stale in minutes, whether writes are queued while degraded and for how long, and each function that stops entirely; the advertised behavior with the same fields as the service advertises them. The signed report gives the record and the advertised behavior, the degraded modes matched both ways, the stale-data limit and the queue hold on each side, the queueing and the functions that stop entirely, and counts them, and names a divergent record: an advertised degraded mode the record does not hold, data served stale longer than advertised, writes refused where the advertised behavior queues them, queued writes held for less time than advertised, and a function the record stops that is not advertised to stop; then modes or queueing the advertised behavior leaves out, a shorter stale limit, a longer hold, an advertised stop the record keeps running and another service, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No modes or no stale-data limit on either side, queueing unstated on either side, or what stops left unstated on either side leaves the record unverified. Minutes compare to the tenth and modes and functions by their words. This reads how a service behaves while partly down, as recorded against what it advertises, and reads no retry design: wever_retry-plan-check, wever_rollback-path-check and wever_failure-notice-check read how a system retries, undoes and announces failures for Agent Recovery, wever_retry-safety-check reads retry safety for Agent Readiness, wever_cache-staleness-check reads an agent’s own context cache design and wever_capacity-queue-check an agent’s work queue against its wait target, while the degradation check reads a service’s degraded modes, stale-data limits, queueing and stops against its advertised behavior. Verdict rely_degradation_divergent, rely_degradation_partial, rely_degradation_unverified or rely_degradation_consistent. POST /api/rely-degradation-check. Reads the reliability records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between documents only: it never probes, pings or measures a live service or endpoint, computes no service credit and names no amount owed, verifies nothing with outside sources and judges no service’s actual reliability, only whether its records agree with each other and with what it advertises, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Reliability reads a service’s reliability records for consistency between documents: an uptime report, an error budget record, a failover arrangement, a dependency disclosure, a degradation behavior record, an incident history, a maintenance record and a periodic reliability report, each against the log, SLO, terms, listing, advertised behavior, buyer disclosure, policy or records it should agree with. Beside it, wever_endpoint-reliability-check and wever_endpoint-honesty-check probe one live endpoint at one moment for the Endpoint reliability page, and the DiligenceOps reads such as wever_sla-evidence-check and wever_status-evidence-check restate one document on its own, while this family connects to nothing and reads the records in the call against each other and against what the service advertises. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-reliability-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-reliability/.
